problem_statement: Trattoria Vesuvio is a neighbourhood wood-fired pizzeria. On the Menu page (menu.html) the static category tabs have been rebuilt into a single interactive 'Tonight's Menu Board' menu-finder: a filter row (All items / Pizzas / Drinks / Burgers / Pasta) sits above one grid of twelve real dishes, with a live readout that reads 'Showing N of 12 - <Category>'. Finish the feature so it is production-grade: (1) the filter row must stay on one readable line on phones without pushing the page wider than the viewport, and the dish grid must lay out as a clean, legible card grid at every width; (2) clicking a category must filter the grid AND recompute the readout to the true visible count and the chosen category label; (3) the shared 'Chef's picks tonight' rail must appear on the Home, Menu and Services pages so the house specials stay visible across the site. Keep every existing section, real menu copy, and the site's warm palette intact with no console errors and no horizontal overflow.
required_content: A 'Tonight's Menu Board' menu-finder on menu.html with a category filter row and one dish grid.
A live readout 'Showing N of 12 - <Category>' that updates to the true visible count on every filter click.
Twelve real dishes across Pizzas, Drinks, Burgers and Pasta with genuine names, descriptions and prices.
A responsive filter row that wraps on phones and a card grid that never overlaps or clips.
A shared 'Chef's picks tonight' rail present on the Home, Menu and Services pages.
Each dish card shows the repo's own food image (pizza, drink, burger or pasta photo) as its thumbnail.
No console errors, no failed network requests, and no horizontal overflow at desktop, tablet or mobile.
design_constraints: Preserve Trattoria Vesuvio's warm cream-and-terracotta palette, card styling and Poppins/Josefin typography.
The menu-finder filter row layout must wrap responsively (never a fixed-width nowrap strip) so it self-clamps on a 390px mobile viewport.
Dish cards must sit in a real wrapping grid with positive spacing; no negative margins, no overlapping cards, no clipped images.
The active filter tab (button) must keep legible contrast (dark label on the highlighted pill), never near-white-on-near-white.
The Chef's picks rail is a presence-only visual element shared across pages; the running count lives only on the menu-finder card grid.
The dish image thumbnails must keep their aspect and spacing at desktop, tablet and mobile widths.

change_completion: The menu-finder renders one grid of 12 dishes with a working category filter row.
Clicking a category filters the grid and the readout shows the true 'Showing N of 12 - <Category>'.
The Chef's picks rail is present on Home, Menu and Services.
design_consistency: The menu-finder and rail match the warm cream/terracotta palette and typography.
The dish grid is a clean, legible card grid with no overlap or contrast failure.
interaction_continuity: The filter click recomputes the visible count rather than leaving a stale headline.
regression: All original sections (hero, about, services, gallery, counter, footer) remain intact.
Real menu copy replaces placeholder lorem; no console errors introduced.
responsive: The filter row wraps on phones with zero horizontal overflow (<=24px).
The dish grid reflows to one/two columns on tablet and mobile without clipping.

metadata.reassign_reason: dedup: repo was shared with slot_141 (lower slot); reassigned to free long-tail restaurant repo.

state_constraints: The home states (desktop_home, mobile_home, tablet_home) capture the scrolled-to-top hero of index.html.
The menu states scroll to #menufinder: desktop_menu and mobile_menu land the filter row and dish grid in frame; desktop_menu_filter is the same page after clicking the Pizzas filter tab.
desktop_services scrolls to the shared .picks-rail and desktop_about captures about.html for cross-page and regression coverage.
author_notes: Trattoria Vesuvio (technext/pizza) menu-finder: the dish cards render the repo's own food images (pizza/drink/burger/pasta photos) as card thumbnails; the responsive card-grid layout, spacing, typography and terracotta theme are the visual assets under test, verified by screenshot anchors at desktop, tablet and mobile widths.
